challenges.active_state_leak: Earlier active paths are entirely resolved before the next outer iteration; state is also local to each function call.
challenges.component_count_reuse: Solved successor counts are reused only when the actual edge reaches that successor. Distinct disconnected cycles are independently seeded; branch merges reuse the correct shared suffix.
challenges.memory_growth: Linear live graph storage with large Python-object constants in reverse_graph. No superlinear graph-sized container construction is present; RSS was not measured.
challenges.premature_cycle_length: Lengths are assigned only after an active-path repeat or a complete lap on the peeled residual cycle. Indegree peeling establishes that its residual lap cannot enter a tail.
challenges.quadratic_path_index: Rejected by aggregate disjoint-path accounting; no empirical timing inference is needed.
challenges.recursion: All five implementations are iterative; no recursive candidate calls. Actual boundary executions completed.

mathematical_review.common_invariant: A forward walk follows edges[v] until a previously encountered vertex. The first repeat on its own active path closes a simple directed cycle. Every cycle node reaches exactly its L cycle vertices. A non-cycle node cannot reappear among its successor reachable vertices, so A[v]=1+A[edges[v]]. A cycle node must be seeded with L before this tail recurrence is used.

edge_walk.aggregate_argument: Discovery and popping each process every node once; additional cycle laps traverse mutually disjoint cycles once in total.
edge_walk.correctness: Three explicit states separate unseen/current/solved. The active encounter is on the current path. A real-edge lap from that vertex counts the closed cycle; popping the path through the encounter vertex resolves exactly that cycle. Remaining tail nodes pop in reverse dependency order. Every active node becomes state 2 before another start.

indegree_peel.aggregate_argument: One edge count/decrement per vertex; each vertex queued/removed at most once. Residual cycles are traversed twice in total, then each removed vertex once.
indegree_peel.auxiliary_space_excluding_output: Theta(n): degree array, removed order and queue
indegree_peel.correctness: Removing indegree-zero nodes cannot remove a cycle vertex. Every non-cycle vertex is eventually removed; the residual functional digraph consists only of disjoint cycles. Count a full forward cycle lap, seed all cycle nodes, then process removed vertices backwards so their successor is solved.

mathematical_review.model: Inferred source proof under valid finite functional digraphs with dense integer labels, no self-loops, and word-RAM O(1) arithmetic/index operations. Counts and indices fit O(log n)-bit words. This is not a machine-checked formal proof.

path_index.aggregate_argument: path.index scans only the current newly discovered path, at most once. Even if it scans almost all of a long chain, no later path can contain those solved vertices. Sum of all scans, slices, deletions and finalizations is O(n).
path_index.auxiliary_space_excluding_output: Theta(n): state array, path and cycle slice
path_index.correctness: Uses explicit 0/1/2 state with the same current-path and solved-successor invariants as signed_walk. Every cycle suffix and reversed tail prefix is marked solved within the same outer iteration.

reverse_graph.aggregate_argument: n predecessor entries, at most n discoveries across all local pos tables, at most n solved/enqueued vertices and n reverse arcs examined. There are n outer starts, including O(1) empty paths. The implementation uses hashed containers, so the strict deterministic array-access guarantee of the other four does not transfer without a hash-cost assumption.
reverse_graph.auxiliary_space_excluding_output: Theta(n): predecessor containers, seen, solved, queue, path and pos
reverse_graph.correctness: parents[v] contains exactly original predecessors u with edges[u]=v. Discovery follows forward edges. Local pos distinguishes a newly closed cycle from a previously seen component. Seed every cycle vertex before reverse propagation; solved blocks all repeat enqueues, including cycle-to-cycle increments. Reverse propagation is predecessor dynamic programming, not a claimed forward walk. seen and solved serve different roles: a reverse-solved tail can later be forward-seen once, without incorrect reseeding or count reuse.
reverse_graph.worst_case_time: Theta(n) graph/hash operations; expected/amortized Theta(n) runtime with O(1) hash operations. Conservative O(n^2) runtime upper bound if individual Python dict/set operations degrade to O(n); tight worst case in the restricted dense-integer domain is not established here.

signed_walk.aggregate_argument: Each node is appended and finalized once. At most one path.index per newly built path; paths are disjoint in newly discovered vertices, so sum of scan lengths <= n. Cycle slices/deletions and reverse-prefix passes also total O(n). Dynamic-array allocation and occasional resizing do not multiply this bound.
signed_walk.auxiliary_space_excluding_output: O(n) path and temporary cycle slice; worst-case Theta(n)
signed_walk.correctness: 0 means unseen, -1 active, positive solved. All path nodes are new. A -1 encounter must belong to this path because earlier iterations resolve every active node. The cycle suffix receives its exact length; reversed prefix then has a solved successor at each assignment. No -1 survives an outer iteration.
